title: The design rules and the Premiere gap report stop pointing at cards that are already answered
goal: On 2026-10-19 every waiting card was taken as recommended and cards became rare, but the design rules runners read and the report that measures Photonz against Premiere still say some questions are open cards. A runner reading them is told to wait for, or open, a card that no longer exists, and the gap report reads further behind than the app is.
notes: Found by the 2026-10-20 digest's rule review. The cards were taken as recommended in 624a8e3a; runner-prompt.md and manager-prompt.md were updated then, the design documents were not. Docs only: no app code, so no walk check is started by it.
acceptance: UX-PATTERNS' Inspector row (docs/design/mocks/shared/UX-PATTERNS.md, line 28) says one main action per section is the rule, instead of calling it the open card 'How many buttons may the right hand panel keep?'

UX-PATTERNS' 'A request that names a system look gets one filmed card' paragraph (around line 117) and the 'decision card before it is built' line (around line 1295) say what runner-prompt.md now says: film both side by side in the audit, choose, and log why

docs/design/video-vs-premiere.md no longer lists the Library on a video as waiting on a card (it shipped on 2026-10-20, a9944834), and row 10 and any other row that says 'waiting on the user's answer' either names the answer taken on 2026-10-20 or is marked closed

grep -n -i 'open card\|waiting on the card\|waiting on the user' over docs/design and docs/design/mocks/shared finds nothing that refers to a card no longer open; the task log pastes the command and its output

log.note: digest 2026-10-25: since 2026-10-24 Command K is Ask on a video (the user's call) and Split at Playhead is Command B. UX-PATTERNS §7 and the gap report's key table already say so, but docs/design/video-vs-premiere.md lines 144 to 147 still count the cut workflow's presses with 'Command K', and the video-beats-premiere success line in queue/objectives.json still lists Command K among the Premiere keys that must do their Premiere job. Both read as a broken promise to a runner checking the bar; fix the counts and flag the objectives line to the manager pass.

triage 2026-10-29: also out of date now: UX-PATTERNS D18 item 4 says a clip dropped between two tracks makes a new track there. Since 2026-10-28 (commits f2f9ac1f, 087b8cb7) a file carried over the timeline also gets a dashed New track row at the top of the tracks and a clip-shaped ghost below them. Name both in D18 while scrubbing, so the next runner building a drop does not invent a fourth way.
